Every market figure carries its own fetched `as of` and is unaffected.

WHY TWO RECOMMENDATIONS AND FIVE WATCHLIST INSTRUCTIONS. Research captured seven distinct candidates. Two are publishable ideas (CVS, ONON). The other five are position management on open positions, and all five carry instructions the schema cannot express as recommendations, so they are on the watchlist with the number as the instruction — not as rejections. VST and RTX are early closes, and there is no field for an exit. HII (stop 265.00 against a 262.00 fill) and ABT (103.20 against 103.00) are profit-protecting stops that sit above the entry of record, which fails validate_report.py's direction_consistency and stop_distance checks because both measure from the fill — the same reason HII was moved to the watchlist on 2026-11-05. XLE's amended stop is correctly ordered but the remaining trade from its 63.90 fill is 1.32:1, below the 2.0 swing floor, so Phase 2d would demote it; a filled entry cannot be re-struck, so the honest choice is hold-with-a-real-stop or close, which is what the note says.

KNOWN TOOLING GAP, carried over from 2026-11-05 and unfixed. A stop amendment reaches state/open_positions.json only through `recommendations`, so the tracker will keep grading HII with no stop, ABT at 97.00 and XLE at 60.80, and the Performance tab will understate the protection actually in place. The closes of VST and RTX will likewise not reach the tracker and those positions will be carried until their stops trade. That is a tooling gap, not a change of mind.

WHY ONE NEW ENTRY IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN A SHORTFALL. Seven setups were built and killed on arithmetic, each logged with its numbers: GDX 0.83:1, GLD 0.87:1, FSLR 0.94:1, NEM 1.60:1, CVS-as-a-swing 1.83:1, AMAT long-term 0.75:1, plus CSCO, GIS, QCOM, CF, GOLD, XLF, IYR and the HCA/CNC fade on fundamentals. The 2026-11-05 volatility shock repriced every ATR in the book, and because the stop floor is denominated in ATRs, a target that cleared 2:1 on Wednesday needs to be ~40% further away today. Both sides of the rotation fail, for opposite reasons: the defensive and value complex that received it (XLF, IYR, XLV, HCA, CNC, PG, KO, COST) sits at or within a few percent of its 200-day highs, so any 2:1 target is a new high, while the de-rated AI complex that funded it has targets far enough away only by assuming a V-shaped recovery six sessions before AMAT reports on 11-12. The report is also deliberately net-reducing: two closes and three stop amendments against one new entry, with 13 positions already open into a 4.4% down day.

RATIOS, CHECKED FOR FITTING. Both published ratios sit modestly above their floors — CVS 2.64 against 2.5, ONON 2.13 against 2.0 — which is the pattern to be suspicious of. The defence is that neither level was set today: CVS's 79.00 entry, 108 target and 68 bear case are unchanged from the 2026-11-05 publication, and ONON's 34.20/41.00/31.00 are unchanged from 2026-11-03, so the targets were not nudged to clear anything. SIZING. CVS is conviction 5 and a long-term core holding, which config/strategy.md would size at 4-5%. It is published at 3% deliberately: this report's long-term record is 0/4 hit target, average -15.2%, and CVS itself was stopped out of a prior conviction-3 long on 2026-11-04. market_context.summary:
The dominant fact of the morning is that the prior session was a crash. On 2026-11-05 SPY fell 4.41% to 733.00 and QQQ fell 6.49% to 647.05 — the worst Nasdaq day in 18 months, with the composite off 5.52% into correction territory, all 11 S&P sectors negative, roughly $2T of market cap erased and about $1T of it in the Mag 7. SMH fell 11.21% and AMD 17.26%. VIXY rose 29.71% and UVXY 45.38%, so this was a genuine volatility event rather than a drift.

The trigger was the 2026 midterms: Democrats took both the House and the Senate, setting up divided government for the final two years of the term, and the market's stated reading is that a Democratic Congress makes the AI datacenter buildout slower, more expensive and more regulated. Wednesday's post-election rally was fully reversed Thursday. The caveat worth holding: a divided Congress legislates very little and the executive levers on AI — tariffs, export controls, permitting — are unchanged, so the legislative risk is largely narrative. The de-rating and the positioning unwind are real regardless.

Two details make the move readable rather than panic. First, it discriminated inside the AI-power trade: the market sold the spending (PWR -12.30%, VRT -14.02%, GEV -7.48%, ETN -7.38%, SMR -14.81%, OKLO -13.20%) and kept the generation (CEG -2.47%, NRG -3.24%, TLN -3.23%), which is a coherent reading of appropriations and permitting bearing on new build rather than on existing megawatts. Second, this was not a flight to quality: on a -4.4% SPY day TLT managed +0.21%, while gold was specifically bid (GLD +0.81%, GDX +1.37%) and healthcare was the defensive winner (XLV -2.50%). Crypto gave no diversification at all, selling with equities (BTC -5.31%, ETH -7.64%).

Macro is hostile to duration and to rate-sensitive equity: the 10-year is 4.90% against a 3.88% funds rate, the 10y-2y curve steepened to +0.38 from +0.32, CPIAUCSL rose 0.65% m/m in September and unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. Nothing reports today or over the weekend; the calendar restarts Monday and the week's decisive event is AMAT on 2026-11-12, the first semicap print after the drawdown.

catalyst.event: Tax-free separation into two independent public companies, announced in the 2026-11-04 8-K and targeted for completion by 2028 — roughly 9,000 retail pharmacies split from Aetna and Caremark. The driver is the re-rating of the remaining insurance-plus-PBM business, not a dated print

recommendations.thesis: CVS fell 12.5% on 2026-11-04 to 79.96 and closed 81.33 on 11-05, and it fell on an announcement rather than a disappointment: the same morning it beat Q3 consensus by 25.4% and raised its outlook while peers rose on the Democratic sweep (ELV +4%, CI +3%). Trailing twelve-month EPS is 1.09 + 2.57 + 2.58 + 2.09 = 8.33, so at 81.33 the stock is 9.8x earnings it has beaten by 8.8%, 15.8%, 38.0% and 25.4% in four consecutive quarters. The separation is the fix for the structural overhang rather than a new risk — Arkansas has barred pharmacy benefit managers from owning pharmacies, Tennessee has passed a similar law, and CVS's own filing warns those laws limit offering both under one roof — so splitting the retail estate from Caremark pre-empts the statute instead of conceding the integrated model failed. A 13x multiple on that same 8.33 is 108, which is not a new high: the stock traded at 110.68 inside the last 200 days.
recommendations.key_risk: INVALIDATION (no hard stop, long-term): federal PBM legislation that materially resets Caremark economics, or two consecutive quarters of adjusted EPS below the consensus the company has beaten four straight times, or abandonment of the separation. A price move alone is not invalidation — at 9.8x the price is the opportunity. The single most likely thing to break it is federal PBM reform, because Caremark is the profit engine that stays with Aetna after the split, and a Democratic Congress is where PBM bills come from. Secondary: a breakup announced for 2028 means two years of distraction, stranded corporate cost and the routine slippage large separations suffer. Disclosed against the idea: zero open-market insider purchases against nine sales worth $359.0M over six months, so there is no confirming buy cluster. ADDED BY RED TEAM, two risks absent from the original: (1) Aetna's medical loss ratio, not PBM reform, is the likeliest route to the 'two consecutive quarters below consensus' invalidation condition — the insurance book is what stays with Caremark after the split, managed-care MLR deterioration has been the sector's defining story, and the four-beat record raises the bar the fifth quarter has to clear because analyst revisions are improving. No figure is quoted because none was fetched this run. (2) A separation resets dividend policy, and CVS is held in part for income; a reduced or split payout at the 2028 completion would force an income-oriented holder base to rotate out, which is a supply overhang independent of whether the thesis is right. Neither is a reason not to own it at 9.8x; both are things that break it that the original key_risk did not name.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that a company announcing a breakup is admitting the integrated model failed, and that the market marked it down 12.5% for exactly that reason while its peers rose. Answered with the statute rather than with optimism: the integrated model is being made illegal state by state, Arkansas first and Tennessee behind it, so separation is compliance arriving ahead of the mandate, and it converts a regulatory discount into two cleanly valued businesses.

watchlist.note: Not a rejection of the business or of the 34.20 level — a rejection of the published 2.13:1. Three legs, any one of which is enough. (1) THE FILL PATH VOIDS THE STOP. Entry 34.20 is 8.9% below the 37.54 close with a dated earnings print on 2026-11-10 in between, so the only route to a fill is a disappointing print — the report says so itself and calls it the pullback-entry trap. Its own key_risk then concedes that in exactly that scenario 'the 31.00 stop is in the path of the gap rather than below it'. A reward-to-risk ratio whose denominator is a stop that cannot hold in the one world where the trade exists is not a ratio. (2) AN HONEST STOP BREAKS THE FLOOR. Recomputed from the fetched ATR14 of 1.4792 on entry 34.20 and target 41.00: the published 31.00 stop is 2.16 ATR, 0.16 ATR above the bare swing floor, and that is the only reason 2.13:1 exists. At the 2.5 ATR guide where this report's stop-outs cluster the stop is 30.50 and the trade is 1.84:1; at 3.0 ATR — the least cushion defensible for a position whose sole entry is through an earnings gap, and the report's own counter_argument concedes the name 'routinely moves several ATRs on earnings' — the stop is 29.76 and the trade is 1.53:1. Both are below the 2.0 swing floor, so widening the stop to one that survives the fill scenario kills the idea, which per CLAUDE.md means it never cleared. (3) THE FILL AND THE TARGET CONTRADICT EACH OTHER. The 41.00 target is 1% under the 41.41 120-day high (fetched). So the trade needs a print bad enough to drop the stock 8.9% to create the entry, and then a round trip to within 1% of its high to pay out. The stated 40% win probability against a 32% break-even prices none of that tension, and the 7.9-point claimed edge was the thinnest in the report. Not killed on: the earnings_date validation warning, which is a genuine source-cap artifact — `earnings --days 14` was re-run and returns ONON 2026-11-10 bmo, consensus 0.4038, exactly as published. Relative strength is also real but rests on a single session (-2.80% against SPY -4.41%), which is an observation rather than a third confirmation.
